questions.question: Why must automation scripts implement rate limiting?
options: To keep cloud bills low
Unattended scripts can hammer targets relentlessly, so respectful pacing must be built in rather than relying on a human to slow down
Because cron jobs cannot run fast commands
Rate limiting is only needed for active exploits
questions.explanation: When a human runs a tool they can stop it; automation runs unattended and repeatedly. Built-in delays and limits keep continuous monitoring from harming targets or getting blocked.

questions.question: In change monitoring, what is a 'baseline'?
options: The minimum number of assets you must monitor
A known-good snapshot of the current state that future scans are compared against to detect changes
The first vulnerability ever found
A list of approved scanning tools
questions.explanation: Change detection works by diffing: you establish a baseline of the current attack surface, then alert on deviations — new subdomains, changed pages, newly opened ports.

questions.question: Why are error handling and logging especially important in ASM automation?
options: They make scripts run faster
Scripts run unattended, so silent failures mean monitoring gaps you won't notice until something is missed
Logs are required to publish scripts on GitHub
Error handling prevents all bugs
questions.explanation: A monitoring script that fails silently gives false confidence — you think you're watching your attack surface but you're not. Logging and error handling make failures visible.

questions.question: What is the typical mechanism for running continuous ASM monitoring?
options: Manually running scans whenever you remember
Scheduled execution via cron jobs or CI/CD pipelines
Asking the hosting provider to notify you of changes
Running one extremely long scan that never finishes
questions.explanation: Continuous monitoring means scheduled, repeatable runs — cron, CI/CD schedules, or workflow templates — producing comparable results over time.

questions.question: What makes an alerting mechanism useful rather than noisy?
options: It sends a notification after every scan regardless of results
It alerts only on meaningful changes, such as new assets or modified services
It only sends alerts during business hours
It emails the entire company for every finding
questions.explanation: Alert fatigue kills monitoring programs. Good alerting is diff-based: notify when something changed or appeared, not on every routine run.
